inspiration: Touch-control layout editor: an in-game grid (default 50 cells, toggled by a command) where buttons are placed, named profiles are saved, and each button has a parameter panel (Documentation/touch-controls.md:11; screenshots Documentation/images/editor.jpg, touch-profiles.jpg, touch-buttons.jpg, not opened). Worth recreating for our 375-wide mobile HUD: snap-to-grid on-device layout editing.

Controls as a data file: the doc says the config lets the user add or change buttons and create custom menus (Documentation/touch-controls.md:5). Idea: ship HUD layouts as data so a layout change needs no code change.

Texture override folders: replacement textures are looked up per map, per common folder, per decal folder and per model name, and one toggle switches them on (Documentation/hd-textures.md:3-9). Idea: a per-zone and per-monster override tier so an artist can swap a look without a code change.

Content kept out of the engine: the engine runs only after the user copies in a separate game folder (README.md:34-37). Idea for us: keep any licensed or borrowed content in a separate pack so the code repo stays clean.

One shader body for several GL dialects: a version-switch preamble (ref/gl/gl2_shim/fragment.glsl.inc:1-5, for example #if VER <= 300 and #define out attribute) wraps the same GLSL source. Idea: write one shader body and generate the variants for a web or mobile target.
